newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips plans sale of Leadframes unit.
newsitem.headline: Philips plans sale of Leadframes unit.

text.p: Philips Semiconductors B.V. is negotiating the sale of unit Philips Leadframes to Alpha Precision Co from Thailand, Philips said on Friday.
"Philips Semiconductors does not consider the production of leadframes as one of its main activities," Philips said in a statement.
Philips Leadframes in Sittard, Netherlands, employs some 170 people. A possible sale of the unit will not have any effect upon employment, Philips said.
Philips declined to give financial details on the expected sale, but said it expected negotiations to be concluded shortly.
"You should think of a couple of weeks, rather than of a couple of months," said a company spokesman.
Alpha Precision Co is part of Bangkok-based Alphatec Electronics Public Co.
The Alphatec Group employs some 8,000 people worldwide and had a two billion guilder turnover in 1996, Philips said.
Philips said Alphatec Electronics Public Co had been an important partner of Philips Semiconductors in the assembling and the testing of integrated circuits in Thailand.
